newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH LAUNCH NEW HIGH-TECH SHARE INDICES.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH LAUNCH NEW HIGH-TECH SHARE INDICES.

text.p: Dutch brokers Wesselius and the Dutch Central Bureau for Statistics (CBS) have launched two new indices to track the performance of domestic high technology companies, Wesselius said on Thursday.
The MIT, or Micro-electronics, Information services and Telecommunications, index numbers 17 Dutch companies active in these areas weighted by market capitalisation.
The MITS, or smallcap, index excludes bourse giants Philips and KPN , which dominate the MIT index with KPN having a weighting of over 40 percent and Philips just over 30.

The indices are based on the price of the constituent shares at the end of 1993 rebased to a hundred. The MIT index stood at 191.1 points on Thursday, while the MITS began at 304.3, reflecting the outperformance of smaller Dutch high tech firms.
"In our view...the index gives an adequate and up-to-date insight into the performance of a dynamic sector as a whole," Wesselius said.
